data_science_governance_definition.description: The role and scope of DSGD (Data Science Governance Definition) is to provide the Data Science-specific domain governance delta used with parent reasoning and behavior governance. It governs analytical objectives, decision targets, population/unit/time scope, dataset and schema identity, data provenance, data quality, hypotheses, method and metric selection, leakage, bias, statistical validity, predictive/causal distinction, analytical claim integrity, run lineage, repair, rerun, analytical status reporting, and Data Science-specific records. DSGD does not replace parent reasoning governance, parent behavior/audit/repair/activation governance, external orchestration, general agentic execution governance, authority governance, software engineering governance, research-governance framing, report-artifact governance, or project coordination governance.

domain_scope.scope_statement: governance of data-science-specific analytical targets, data state, methods, metrics, claim validity, evaluation failure modes, repair origins, reruns, and analytical records for LLMs, analytical agents, agentic AI workflows, and human analytical processes

abstraction_and_context_policy.purpose: prevent data-science domain rules from becoming case-specific implementation, company, tool, or platform rules while allowing local specificity when needed to preserve analytical meaning

role_complete_separation.principle: DSGD must govern data-science-specific analytical validity, data state, method validity, claim integrity, run lineage, and repair/rerun conditions without absorbing parent governance, sibling domain responsibilities, or external orchestration.

separation_targets.source_material: datasets, schemas, logs, reports, prior records, observations, or references used for analysis; source content is not absorbed by default
separation_targets.domain_definition: data-science-specific rules, checks, failures, repair origins, records, and responsibility boundaries
separation_targets.inherited_governance: ARGD and DAGD remain authoritative for general reasoning and general behavior/audit/repair/activation governance
separation_targets.sibling_reference: AAGD, DAAGD, SEGD, AIRGD, ACRGD, PMOGD, and other domains are referenced only when boundary conditions are material
separation_targets.governed_target: analytical objective, data, method, metric, claim, run, repair, rerun, or analytical record
separation_targets.domain_evaluation: Data Science-specific checks and evaluation dimensions defined as domain delta only
separation_targets.domain_repair: Data Science-specific repair origins and revalidation scopes, not the parent repair cycle itself
separation_targets.activation: local applicability signals only; routing and priority remain external
separation_targets.status_reporting: Data Science status delta only, not broad runtime status replacement
separation_targets.records: Analysis Process Record and Evaluation/Audit Record remain separate from metadata and orchestration
separation_targets.external_orchestration: routing, registry, priority, and activation orchestration remain external
separation_targets.metadata: identity, authorship, license, repository, and compatibility information remain metadata, not domain rules

cross_domain_interference_policy.purpose: prevent DSGD from absorbing neighboring domains while preserving explicit handoff conditions for overlapping data-science workflows

declared_overlap_boundaries.aagd: DSGD reports analytical agentic conditions that affect data, method, metric, claim, run, or evidence lineage; general agentic execution remains AAGD.
declared_overlap_boundaries.daagd: DSGD reports authority uncertainty conditions; authority, approval, and responsibility decisions remain DAAGD.
declared_overlap_boundaries.segd: DSGD governs analytical run validity and traceability; implementation, code, build, test, and repository artifact quality remain SEGD.
declared_overlap_boundaries.airgd: DSGD governs data, statistics, predictive/causal validity, and analytical claim controls; research novelty, prior work, and publication claim framing remain AIRGD.
declared_overlap_boundaries.acrgd: DSGD governs analytical claim integrity; artifact composition, readability, and publication readiness remain ACRGD.
declared_overlap_boundaries.pmogd: DSGD governs analytical run repair/rerun lineage; owners, deadlines, milestones, blockers, and delivery coordination remain PMOGD.

group_descriptions.problem_scope_and_decision_definition: Capabilities for converting an analytical request into an explicit objective, decision target, population, unit, and time scope without silently collapsing alternative formulations.
group_descriptions.data_understanding_and_validation: Capabilities for inspecting schema, profiling data state, and identifying quality conditions that affect method choice or claim validity.
group_descriptions.provenance_and_lineage: Capabilities for tracing datasets, transformations, experiments, and reruns across the analytical lifecycle.
group_descriptions.analytical_reasoning_and_method_control: Capabilities for preserving hypotheses, selecting methods with stated basis, checking assumptions, and distinguishing predictive from causal reasoning.
group_descriptions.risk_and_validity_control: Capabilities for detecting leakage, bias, uncertainty, and validity threats that can invalidate a result.
group_descriptions.claim_repair_and_rerun_control: Capabilities for classifying analytical claims, locating repair origins, managing reruns, and reporting analytical state.
group_descriptions.advanced_data_and_model_monitoring: Capabilities for automated monitoring of distribution, regression, feature lineage, and model lineage.
group_descriptions.advanced_falsification_and_causal_assess: Capabilities for generating counter-hypotheses and assessing causal identification requirements.
group_descriptions.advanced_execution_and_recovery: Capabilities for scoped reruns, checkpoint recovery, side-effect-safe retries, and human escalation.
group_descriptions.comparative_audit_and_artifact_integrity: Capabilities for comparing runs, localizing failures, and verifying artifact identity.

problem_and_decision_definition.purpose: Separate the originating request from the analytical question and define the decision or action the analysis is intended to support.

scope_population_and_unit_definition.purpose: Define the analytical subject, population, unit, time scope, comparison basis, and target or outcome when_applicable.

data_intake_and_provenance.purpose: Identify datasets and establish data identity, version, source, collection context, access constraints, and provenance limits.

data_quality_and_schema_assessment.purpose: Assess schema compatibility, missingness, duplication, outliers, units, granularity, temporal alignment, label state, and known collection bias.

hypothesis_and_analysis_plan.purpose: Define hypotheses, counter-hypotheses, falsification targets, assumptions, candidate methods, decision criteria, and branch conditions.

preprocessing_and_feature_design.purpose: Define and execute transformations and feature design while preserving lineage and preventing leakage.

method_selection_and_baseline.purpose: Select methods and baselines under explicit criteria, assumptions, constraints, and comparable evaluation conditions.

execution_and_experiment_tracking.purpose: Execute the analysis or model while tracking run identity, data references, code or configuration, versions, seeds, tool calls, checkpoints, and outputs.

evaluation_and_validation.purpose: Evaluate analytical results against predefined metrics, baselines, assumptions, robustness conditions, leakage controls, bias controls, and regression criteria.

interpretation_and_claim_control.purpose: Convert results into explicitly classified claims without exceeding the evidence type, scope, uncertainty, or causal identification supported by the analysis.

reporting_and_decision_support.purpose: Report objectives, data, methods, results, uncertainty, limitations, failures, and decision implications with sufficient traceability for review and reuse.

audit_repair_and_rerun.purpose: Audit the full run, localize failures, select repair origin, preserve prior history, rerun the affected scope, compare before and after states, and re-fix governance.

self_check_questions: Did I separate the originating request from the analytical question?
Did I define the decision target, population, unit of analysis, and time scope?
Did I fix dataset and schema identity and version?
Did I disclose provenance limits and data quality conditions?
Did I preserve hypotheses, counter-hypotheses, and falsification targets?
Did I state the method selection basis, baseline, and excluded alternatives?
Did I check target, temporal, split, and preprocessing leakage where applicable?
Did I assess sampling, selection, measurement, and distribution risks where applicable?
Did I distinguish observation, estimate, prediction, association, causation, interpretation, and recommendation?
Did I disclose the evaluation dataset, metrics, uncertainty, and limitations?
Did I avoid allowing an aggregate score to override a critical invalidation?
Did I preserve run lineage and prior run immutability?
Did I identify the repair origin and affected downstream artifacts?
Did I record rerun scope and before-after differences?
Did I preserve agent role, tool, checkpoint, handoff, and approval traces when_applicable?

repair.purpose: define data-science-specific repair origins, affected analytical scopes, revalidation targets, rerun lineage, and review condition findings without replacing the parent repair cycle

analysis_process_record.purpose: Record what was analyzed, why, under which data and assumptions, by which process, with which branches, results, evidence, uncertainty, and rerun conditions.

evaluation_audit_record.purpose: Record how an analytical run was evaluated, where and why it failed, what was invalidated, how it was repaired, and what rerun state resulted.
